questions.q: Why do OrderManagement and DriverHR move to Azure SQL Managed Instance rather than Azure SQL Database?
options: They depend on cross-database queries and a SQL Server Agent job — both unsupported on Azure SQL Database, but supported on Managed Instance
Managed Instance is always cheaper than Azure SQL Database
Azure SQL Database doesn't support encryption of any kind
There is no real difference between the two options for this scenario
questions.explain: Cross-database queries and Agent jobs are the specific, stated dependencies that rule out Azure SQL Database for these two databases.

questions.q: Why does Telemetry get a different deployment target (Azure SQL Database, Hyperscale) instead of also moving to Managed Instance?
options: It has no cross-database dependency and is a single, fast-growing, append-heavy table — exactly the workload Hyperscale is built for, without needing Managed Instance's extra surface area
Hyperscale is required for any database over 1 GB
Telemetry also needs SQL Server Agent, so it must match the others
All three databases must always use the same deployment target for consistency
questions.explain: Applying one deployment model to every workload regardless of its actual dependencies is the mistake this lesson explicitly avoids.

questions.q: Why does the SSN/license data get Always Encrypted specifically, rather than relying on Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) alone?
options: TDE only protects data at rest (on disk and in backups); Always Encrypted keeps the plaintext unreadable even to a DBA running an ad hoc query against the live table — which is the actual risk Compliance named
TDE and Always Encrypted do exactly the same thing, so either works
Always Encrypted is only used for numeric columns
TDE is not available on Managed Instance
questions.explain: Compliance's worry was about who can read the value, not just disk theft — that's specifically what Always Encrypted addresses and TDE alone doesn't.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose an online migration approach for OrderManagement instead of an offline backup/restore?
options: Ops stated that the 7-9am dispatch window can't go down, and offline migration requires a maintenance window that would violate that constraint
Online migration is always faster regardless of the constraints
Offline migration is not a real option in Azure at all
Online migration requires no validation after cutover
questions.explain: The migration approach is chosen to fit the stated business constraint, not chosen by default — online migration keeps the database serving traffic through the cutover.

questions.q: Besides confirming the application reconnected, what does this lesson say to validate after the migration cutover?
options: Row counts and checksums against the source, plus a smoke test of the specific dispatch query that was timing out
Nothing further — a successful app connection is sufficient validation
Only that the server name resolves in DNS
Re-running the entire migration from scratch as a check
questions.explain: "The app connected" doesn't confirm the data or the previously-slow query actually behave correctly post-migration — concrete validation does.
